/-!
# Types (model theory): models omitting countably many types

A *type* (over the empty set) in the free variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ is a set of
first-order formulas whose free variables lie among $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. A structure
$\mathcal{M}$ *omits* the type if no $n$-tuple of elements of $\mathcal{M}$ satisfies every
formula in it.

Assume $K$ is the class of models of a countable first order theory omitting countably many
types. If $K$ has a model of cardinality $\aleph_{\omega_1}$, does it have a model of cardinality
continuum?

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics#Model_theory_and_formal_languages)
- [Wikipedia, Type (model theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_%28model_theory%29)
- [S. Shelah, *Borel sets with large squares*, Fund. Math. 159 (1999), 1–50](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9802134)
-/

def Omits (M : Type*) [L.Structure M] {n : ℕ} (p : Set (L.Formula (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ v : Fin n → M, ∀ φ ∈ p, φ.Realize v
blocks.docstring:
A structure `M` *omits* the (partial) type `p`, a set of `L`-formulas in the free variables
`x_0, …, x_{n-1}`, if no `n`-tuple of elements of `M` satisfies every formula in `p`.
No consistency requirement is imposed on `p`: a set of formulas that is inconsistent with the
ambient theory is omitted by every model of it.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FirstOrder.Language.Theory.realizedTypes / Theory.CompleteType (complete types only, via the expanded language L[[α]]; would exclude partial types); FirstOrder.Language.Formula.Realize (used as the building block).
justification.name: Types.Omits
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has `Theory.realizedTypes` only for complete types (`Theory.CompleteType`), and no predicate saying a structure omits/realizes an arbitrary set of formulas in finitely many free variables. `Omits M p := ¬ ∃ v : Fin n → M, ∀ φ ∈ p, φ.Realize v`.

justification.name: Types.modelsOmitting
justification.why_needed: Names the class K of the statement: the set of bundled models `T.ModelType` omitting every type in the family Γ, so that the hypothesis and conclusion read `∃ M ∈ modelsOmitting T Γ, #M = _`.

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem omits_iff (M : Type*) [L.Structure M] {n : ℕ} (p : Set (L.Formula (Fin n))) :
    Omits M p ↔ ∀ v : Fin n → M, ∃ φ ∈ p, ¬ φ.Realize v := by
  simp [Omits]

blocks.text:
/--
Assume $K$ is the class of models of a countable first order theory $T$ omitting countably many
types. If $K$ has a model of cardinality $\aleph_{\omega_1}$, does it have a model of cardinality
continuum $2^{\aleph_0}$?

Here a countable first order theory is a theory in a language with countably many symbols, and
a type is any set of formulas (over the empty set) in finitely many free variables, complete
or partial. `answer(True)` means that the answer is "yes" for every such $T$ and family of types.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem types :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) [Countable L.Symbols] (T : L.Theory)
      (Γ : Set (Σ n : ℕ, Set (L.Formula (Fin n)))), Γ.Countable →
      (∃ M ∈ modelsOmitting.{u, v, w} T Γ, #M = ℵ_ ω₁) →
      ∃ M ∈ modelsOmitting.{u, v, w} T Γ, #M = 𝔠 := by
  sorry

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question (Shelah's Hanf-number-type problem, cited by Wikipedia to 'Borel sets with large squares'): for every countable language L, L-theory T and countable family of types (sets of L-formulas in finitely many free variables, over the empty set, complete or partial), if some model of T omitting all of them simultaneously has cardinality ℵ_{ω₁} (`Cardinal.aleph ω₁`), then some such model has cardinality 𝔠 = 2^{ℵ₀} (`Cardinal.continuum`); implicit universal quantifiers over L, T and the family, and both hypothesis and conclusion are existentials over models in K; subtlety: read literally the answer appears to follow from Morley's omitting-types theorem plus downward Löwenheim–Skolem (the source may intend a stronger, 'absolutely generated' model of size continuum), but the formalization should follow the statement as posed, with answer(True) meaning 'yes'.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same literal reading and agree on every semantic point: countable first-order theory = theory in a language with `Countable L.Symbols` (equivalent to `L.card ≤ ℵ₀`, the idiom of Wikipedia/VaughtConjecture.lean; every theory in such a language is countable); 'countably many types' = an at-most-countable family of sets of `L.Formula (Fin n)` (types over ∅ in finitely many variables, partial or complete); omission = no `Fin n`-tuple realizes every formula simultaneously (for n = 0 this degenerates correctly to 'M fails some sentence of p'); models = Mathlib's bundled nonempty `Theory.ModelType`; exact cardinalities `#M = ℵ_ ω₁` (verified by `rfl` to be `Cardinal.aleph (Ordinal.omega 1)`) and `#M = 𝔠` (`Cardinal.continuum`); question style `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ L T Γ, (∃ M ∈ K, #M = ℵ_{ω₁}) → ∃ M ∈ K, #M = 𝔠`, so `answer(True)` = 'yes'. Omitting the consistency requirement on the formula sets (c02–c07) is equivalent to imposing it (c01 via CompleteType extension, c08 via finite satisfiability): inconsistent sets are omitted by every model of T, so removing them leaves K unchanged. Both existentials range over the same universe `w`; since the language is countable and ℵ_{ω₁}, 𝔠 are small in every universe, this is universe-independent. c06 was chosen as the base because its bespoke `modelsOmitting T Γ` mirrors the informal 'class K' most directly, making the theorem read exactly like the source. Edits: added the `omits_iff` API lemma (from c04/c07), changed the concrete sanity lemmas to `category test`, added the Shelah arXiv reference and section anchor for the Wikipedia list, and clarified in the `Omits` docstring that no consistency condition is imposed. Rejected: c05 (AMS 03 lint warning under repo options, weaker references), c02 (docstring contains a proof-sketch/review note about the downward Löwenheim–Skolem case, which AGENTS.md forbids in Lean files), c01 (more convoluted indexed-family/CompleteType encoding and universe `max u v w`, no gain in faithfulness), c03/c08 (non-idiomatic `(_ : Countable L.Symbols)` binder; otherwise fine).

context: In model theory and related areas of mathematics, a type is an object that describes how a (real or possible) element or finite collection of elements in a mathematical structure might behave.  More precisely, it is a set of first-order formulas in a language L with free variables x1, x2,..., xn that are true of a set of n-tuples of an L-structure ${\mathcal {M}}$.  Depending on the context, types can be complete or partial and they may use a fixed set of constants, A, from the structure ${\mathcal {M}}$.  The question of which types represent actual elements of ${\mathcal {M}}$ leads to the ideas of saturated models and omitting types.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The table's single slot and its notes (partial-or-complete types over the empty set, countable language, existentials over K in both hypothesis and conclusion, answer(True) = yes, follow the statement as posed despite the apparent triviality under Morley + Löwenheim–Skolem) were followed exactly.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Types (model theory): models omitting countably many types

A *type* (over the empty set) in the free variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ is a set of
first-order formulas whose free variables lie among $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. A structure
$\mathcal{M}$ *omits* the type if no $n$-tuple of elements of $\mathcal{M}$ satisfies every
formula in it.

Assume $K$ is the class of models of a countable first order theory omitting countably many
types. If $K$ has a model of cardinality $\aleph_{\omega_1}$, does it have a model of cardinality
continuum?

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics#Model_theory_and_formal_languages)
- [Wikipedia, Type (model theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_%28model_theory%29)
- [S. Shelah, *Borel sets with large squares*, Fund. Math. 159 (1999), 1–50](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9802134)
-/

universe u v w

open Cardinal FirstOrder.Language
open scoped Ordinal

namespace Types

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}}

/-- A structure `M` *omits* the (partial) type `p`, a set of `L`-formulas in the free variables
`x_0, …, x_{n-1}`, if no `n`-tuple of elements of `M` satisfies every formula in `p`.
No consistency requirement is imposed on `p`: a set of formulas that is inconsistent with the
ambient theory is omitted by every model of it. -/
def Omits (M : Type*) [L.Structure M] {n : ℕ} (p : Set (L.Formula (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ v : Fin n → M, ∀ φ ∈ p, φ.Realize v

/-- The class `K` of models of the theory `T` that omit every type in the family `Γ`.
Each member of `Γ` is a type in some finite number `n` of free variables. -/
def modelsOmitting (T : L.Theory) (Γ : Set (Σ n : ℕ, Set (L.Formula (Fin n)))) :
    Set (Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T) :=
  {M | ∀ p ∈ Γ, Omits M p.2}

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem omits_iff (M : Type*) [L.Structure M] {n : ℕ} (p : Set (L.Formula (Fin n))) :
    Omits M p ↔ ∀ v : Fin n → M, ∃ φ ∈ p, ¬ φ.Realize v := by
  simp [Omits]

/-- Every structure omits the inconsistent type `{⊥}`. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem omits_singleton_bot (M : Type*) [L.Structure M] (n : ℕ) :
    Omits M ({⊥} : Set (L.Formula (Fin n))) := by
  simp [Omits]

/-- No nonempty structure omits the empty type. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem not_omits_empty (M : Type*) [L.Structure M] [Nonempty M] (n : ℕ) :
    ¬ Omits M (∅ : Set (L.Formula (Fin n))) := by
  simp [Omits]

/-- Every model of `T` belongs to the class of models of `T` omitting no types. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem mem_modelsOmitting_empty (T : L.Theory) (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T) :
    M ∈ modelsOmitting T ∅ := by
  simp [modelsOmitting]

/--
Assume $K$ is the class of models of a countable first order theory $T$ omitting countably many
types. If $K$ has a model of cardinality $\aleph_{\omega_1}$, does it have a model of cardinality
continuum $2^{\aleph_0}$?

Here a countable first order theory is a theory in a language with countably many symbols, and
a type is any set of formulas (over the empty set) in finitely many free variables, complete
or partial. `answer(True)` means that the answer is "yes" for every such $T$ and family of types.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem types :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) [Countable L.Symbols] (T : L.Theory)
      (Γ : Set (Σ n : ℕ, Set (L.Formula (Fin n)))), Γ.Countable →
      (∃ M ∈ modelsOmitting.{u, v, w} T Γ, #M = ℵ_ ω₁) →
      ∃ M ∈ modelsOmitting.{u, v, w} T Γ, #M = 𝔠 := by
  sorry

end Types

items: Literal reading followed, as instructed by the decomposition notes: both hypothesis and conclusion are plain existentials over the class K of models omitting Γ, with exact cardinality equalities `#M = ℵ_ ω₁` and `#M = 𝔠`. The note that this literal reading may follow from Morley's omitting-types theorem plus downward Löwenheim–Skolem (and that Shelah may intend an 'absolutely generated' continuum-size model) is NOT encoded; the file follows the statement as posed.

A 'type' is any set of L-formulas in finitely many free variables `Fin n`, over the empty set (no parameters), partial or complete; consistency with T is not required. This is equivalent to requiring consistency, since a set of formulas inconsistent with T is omitted by every model of T, so dropping such members from Γ leaves the class K (and countability of Γ) unchanged.

'Countably many types' is read as an at-most-countable family `Γ : Set (Σ n : ℕ, Set (L.Formula (Fin n)))` with `Γ.Countable` (finite, including empty, families allowed; Γ = ∅ gives the trivially true LS case and is harmless).

'Countable first order theory' is read as a theory in a language with countably many symbols (`Countable L.Symbols`), following the existing `Wikipedia/VaughtConjecture.lean`; then T is automatically countable.

Models are bundled `T.ModelType.{u, v, w}` (nonempty models); the hypothesised ℵ_{ω₁}-sized model and the sought 𝔠-sized model live in the same universe `w`. The theorem is universe polymorphic in u, v, w.

`ℵ_ ω₁` requires `open scoped Ordinal` (the `ω₁` notation is scoped in `Ordinal`, not `Cardinal`); without it `ω₁` was silently auto-bound as a free variable. Verified via `#print` that the statement elaborates to `Cardinal.aleph (Ordinal.omega 1)`.
Used `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ...` question style per CONTRIBUTING.md; `answer(True)` means 'yes'.

reviewer_notes: Source ambiguity: the Wikipedia list entry is a compressed form of Shelah's question in 'Borel sets with large squares' [Sh:522], which asks for a model of cardinality continuum 'generated in a nice, absolute way'. Per the decomposition notes, the file formalizes the entry as posed (plain existence of a continuum-sized model in K). Note on the decomposition's remark that the literal statement 'appears to follow from Morley plus downward LS': as c02 correctly objects, downward Löwenheim–Skolem settles only the case 2^{ℵ₀} ≤ ℵ_{ω₁} (omission of types over ∅ is preserved under elementary substructures), while Morley's omitting-types theorem needs a model of size ≥ ℶ_{ω₁}, which ℵ_{ω₁} does not provide when 2^{ℵ₀} > ℵ_{ω₁}; so the literal statement is not trivially provable in Lean and is a legitimate open statement. 'Countable first order theory' is read as a theory in a countable language; reading it instead as a countable set of sentences in a possibly uncountable language gives an equivalent problem (restrict to the countably many symbols occurring in T and the types; expansions do not change cardinality). Final file compiled with `lake env lean --json` and also with the lakefile's `autoImplicit=false` and all weak linter options; the only diagnostic is `declaration uses 'sorry'` on the main theorem. The `#print` of the theorem shows `answer(sorry)` as `True`; this is the repository's `answer()` elaborator default for Prop-valued answers, not an edit.
